content.text: Can you show geometrically why the functional equation and complex conjugation produce the fourfold symmetry of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function?

## The two symmetries become diagonal

Work with Riemann's completed zeta function

\[
\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma\!\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)\zeta(s),
\]

which satisfies both

\[
\xi(s)=\xi(1-s),\qquad\xi(\overline{s})=\overline{\xi(s)}.
\]

Center the plane on the critical line by writing \(s=\frac12+x+iy\), and let \(u=(x,y)^{\mathsf T}\). Complex conjugation \(C\) and the functional-equation reflection \(F\) act by

\[
C:u\longmapsto
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}u,\qquad
F:u\longmapsto
\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}u.
\]

They are already diagonal, so they commute. Their product is the reflection across the critical line:

\[
FC:u\longmapsto
\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}u.
\]

Hence a nontrivial zero \(\rho=\sigma+it\) generates the orbit

\[
\boxed{\rho,\quad\overline{\rho},\quad1-\rho,\quad1-\overline{\rho}}.
\]

The quartet collapses to a conjugate pair precisely on the fixed set of \(FC\):

\[
\rho=1-\overline{\rho}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Re}\rho=\frac12.
\]

**This is the geometric content of the Riemann Hypothesis:** every nontrivial zero is conjectured to lie on that fixed line. The symmetry itself explains the orbit; it does not prove that every orbit collapses.
